Gain-of-function mutations in MAP2K1 (MEK1), a key component of the RAS-MAPK pathway, lead to its constitutive activation. This hyperactivation of the RAS-MAPK signaling pathway can manifest differently depending on the cellular context. In osteoblasts, it contributes to the abnormal bone deposition seen in melorheostosis (HP:0000924). In other cell types, this same pathway dysregulation, often driven by mutations in upstream genes like HRAS or BRAF, results in the pleiotropic developmental effects characteristic of RASopathies, including intellectual disability (HP:0001249) and facial dysmorphism (HP:0001999).
